Rates and Your Bill
We’re committed to delivering reliable electricity while keeping bills as low as possible.
The bill you pay each month is determined by the amount of electricity you use and by rates approved by the Florida Public Service Commission (PSC).
The links below will help you understand the components of your bill and find ways to save.
Discover ways to save
Aside from rates, your monthly bill amount is determined by the amount of electricity used. Find out how simple changes can help you save.
Start saving
Business programs
Bill payment assistance
Our advocacy partners help us secure federal funding to help low-income customers receive financial assistance with their electric bills.

How to read your bill
1 Bill-specific information:
a. Service period dates: The service days included in
this bill. Note: The number of days in a billing 1
period may fluctuate due to weekends, holidays or
changes in the date we read your meter.
b. Statement date: The date upon which the monthly
bill is generated.
c. Account number: This is a unique identifier for the 2
customer at this address – refer to this number if 7
3
you contact FPL about your account.
d. Service address: The location where electricity is
being provided. 8
4
2 Total amount due: The amount you owe for services
already used during the billing period, plus any outstanding
service charges, deposits or late payment fees incurred.
5
3 New charges due by: When the payment for new charges
is due.
4 Bill summary: A high-level summary of the total amount 6
due and payments received during the service period
indicated on your bill.
5 Bill messages: Important and timely information that can
benefit our customers. 9
10
6 How to contact FPL: You can manage your account, make
a payment, report an outage and more at FPL.com, or you
can call us.
7 Energy usage history: Illustrates the monthly kilowatt-
hours (kWh) used for the last 13 months.
8 Keep in mind: Important information that can benefit
our customers.
Stay connected
9 Customer contact information: Name associated For a fast, easy way to stay informed and report
with the account and the address requested to have
outages, download the FPL Mobile App.
communications sent.
FPL.com/MobileApp
10 Payment mailing address: Location to send a check
payment for this bill. For more payment options, visit
FPL.com/WaysToPay.

How to read your bill

a. Service period dates: The service days included in
this bill. Note: The number of days in a billing 1
period may fluctuate due to weekends, holidays or
changes in the date we read your meter.
b. Statement date: The date upon which the monthly
bill is generated.
c. Account number: This is a unique identifier for the 2
customer at this address – refer to this number if 7
3
you contact FPL about your account.
d. Service address: The location where electricity is
being provided. 8
4
2 Total amount due: The amount you owe for services
already used during the billing period, plus any outstanding
service charges, deposits or late payment fees incurred.
5
3 New charges due by: When the payment for new charges
is due.
4 Bill summary: A high-level summary of the total amount 6
due and payments received during the service period
indicated on your bill.
5 Bill messages: Important and timely information that can
benefit our customers. 9
10
6 How to contact FPL: You can manage your account, make
a payment, report an outage and more at FPL.com, or you

How to read your bill (continued)
11 Rate: Determines how the bill is calculated – for this
account, RS-1 for residential service.
12 Electric service amount: These charges are regulated
by the Florida Public Service Commission. The total 14
electric service amount is made up of the following
charges:
a. Base charge: A fixed monthly amount to cover the 11
cost of providing service to your location. This 15
charge includes the cost of the meter, billing and
12
providing customer service. It is applicable whether
or not electricity is used.
13
b. Non-fuel charge: This total charge is made up of
base rates and the following charges:
» Energy Conservation Cost Recovery Charge
(ECCR): Cost of programs designed to reduce
electric demand and consumption.
» Capacity Cost Recovery Clause (CCRC):
Cost for purchasing electricity from non-
FPL-owned resources, as well as certain
nuclear-related expenses.
» Environmental Cost Recovery Clause
(ECRC): Cost to meet environmental laws and
regulations.
16
» Storm Protection Plan Cost Recovery
Clause (SPPCRC): Cost to strengthen the grid
in order to reduce restoration costs and

Time-of-Use (TOU) rates
Learn about TOU rates during peak and off-peak hours and see if you qualify.
How it works
Unlike traditional rates where the cost is always the same, TOU rates reflect the fluctuating demand for electricity. During peak hours, the cost is about 26 cents per kilowatt-hour, while off-peak hours cost around 9 cents.*
See standard rates
* This is an approximation and may vary by location.
Enrollment terms and limitations
Requires annual commitment
Enrollment takes about three months
Requires a new meter
You may need to be present for installation if meter is inaccessible
No extra cost to join TOU (same as standard service)
Cannot participate in FPL On Call,
®
FPL Budget Billing
®
or FPL EVolution
®
Is a TOU rate plan right for you?
To realize savings, customers must use less energy during the “peak” hours.
Rodney:
Uses over 1,000 kWh of energy per month
Sets the A/C to 78 degrees or higher during peak hours
Has no one home during peak hours Monday-Friday
Uses timers to run small appliances during off-peak times
Rodney travels for work and owns an EV that he only charges during off-peak hours, he may save on the TOU rate.
Valerie:
Uses less than 1000 kwh per month
Sets the A/C to lower than 78 degrees during peak hours
Works from home and is mostly at home during the day Monday-Friday
Has no timers and runs washer, dryer, pool pump, or other appliances during the day
With lower energy usage, and being home during peak hours, Valerie would not save on the TOU rate.
Timing is everything
To benefit from TOU, you must shift electricity use away from peak hours. *
Summer
April 1 to Oct. 31
Winter
Nov. 1 to March 31
* Excludes weekends, New Year’s Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day.

Frequently Asked Questions
How will I know if the program will benefit me?
By filling out the form below, a rate analysis can be performed comparing your energy consumption profile to the “peak” and “off-peak” time periods. This analysis will help you determine whether or not the rate is a good fit for your home.
What if I go on the program and later decide it’s not a good fit?
The minimum enrollment period is one year. After the first year, customers have the option to exit the program.
Can I check my usage an
[DOC 7] https://www.fpl.com/rates/time-of-use.html
d rate mid-month to make sure I’m meeting my savings goals?
With the free FPL Energy Manager, you're able to monitor, analyze and simulate your energy usage so you can save on your bill.
As part of the Energy Manager you also have access to the Energy Analyzer, Energy Dashboard, Appliance Calculators, and Simulator tools. Together, they can help you identify changes to help lower your bill.
Start now
Will I be notified when the TOU rates/times change season to season?
Important information that can benefit our customers will be found on the billing statement within the keep in mind section. Review your preferences to ensure your signed up for ‘special updates’ to receive our newsletter.
